title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Zarnuki
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Sanhedrin 26a relates that he went with Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak (II) to intercalate the year. In Asya, Resh Lakish met them and joined them; he said, “I will go and see how they act.” He (Resh Lakish) saw a man plowing and said to them, “A Kohen, and plowing?” They said to him, “He can say,” etc. When they arrived there, they went up to the roof and pulled the ladder out from under him (so that Resh Lakish would not come up). He came before Rabbi Yochanan and said to him: “Are people suspected regarding the Sabbatical year fit to intercalate the year?” Then he said, “It is not difficult for me; it is like the three cowherds…” When they came before Rabbi Yochanan they said to him: “He called us cowherds, and the Master said nothing to him?” He said to them: “And if he had called you shepherds, what would I have said to him?”

notes.text: The cowherd/shepherd exchange and ladder episode remain distinct speakers. Yehotzadak is not silently normalized to another patronymic.
